coverageNote.note: Boston Beer (Sam Adams, Truly, Twisted Tea) operates ~5 NA breweries + 1 UK; we audited the NA breweries.

account.dossierIntro: Boston Beer Company runs Sam Adams plus the cidery and seltzer brands. 6 production sites; we audited 5. The Cincinnati Brewery runs the largest dock-door count in the network. Angry Orchard Walden NY is 75.6 acres of apple-cider innovation. Multi-brand brewing means the yard handles 4 distinct SKU velocities. YardFlow runs them as 4 parallel queues on one protocol.
surprisingFindings: Angry Orchard Walden NY is 75.6 acres of cider innovation. Different yard rhythm than the beer plants.
5 of 5 audited sites run their own dock-handling. Boston Beer never outsourced shipping.
71 dock doors across 5 audited sites. Premium craft means slow turn, high margin.

sites.name: Samuel Adams Pennsylvania Brewery - Breinigsville PA
sites.type: Brewery / production facility (largest in network; includes ~1M sq ft brewery + warehouse space on ~76 acres)

steps.step: Route to correct building / drop yard

sites.dossierExcerpt:
The roster's ROOFTOP geocode (40.5752, -75.624758) landed in a gap between
buildings in the Penn Drive industrial park. Probing satellite at z16-z18 around
the point identified the correct building ~400 m to the WNW: a large
manufacturing complex with the unmistakable signature of a brewery — a dense
cluster of cylindrical fermentation/bright tanks in the NW, brewing process
equipment, grain silos, a complex multi-section roof with heavy rooftop
mechanical equipment, an employee parking lot, and a taproom patio with brick
pavers and picnic landscaping on the NE corner. Web research (Lehigh Valley
Chamber, Yelp, Panjiva import records) confirms Boston Beer / Samuel Adams
operates the Pennsylvania Brewery at 7880 Penn Dr. The neighboring large white
buildings to the SW and SE are separate distribution warehouses, not part of

fieldNotes.truckGate: Driver reviews explicitly describe a manned front gate and check-in; satellite shows a fully fenced perimeter with controlled access. Street View does not reach the brewery's internal truck gate, but the gate is corroborated by web research.
fieldNotes.guardShack: Driver reviews reference 'guard shack personnel' and 'professional front-gate staff' at this brewery — staffed guard booth confirmed.
fieldNotes.scale: Driver reviews state 'Samuel Adams Brewery delivers convenient on-site scales, and weigh-ins at the property' — on-site truck scale confirmed.
fieldNotes.multiStep: Gate check-in plus a separate on-site scale/weigh-in step before docks implies a two-stage process; flagged medium-confidence as the scale house was not isolated in imagery.
fieldNotes.dockDoorCount: ~40 estimated across multiple building faces (east dock apron plus loading along the trailer-yard faces); large brewery with extensive trailers backed in. Approximate.
fieldNotes.dropArea: Extensive multi-row trailer drop yards on the south and west sides — well over 50 trailer stalls visible.
fieldNotes.fastLaneOpportunity: Large paved yard aprons and wide internal drives give physical room to add an express/bypass lane.
fieldNotes.shipRcvSeparate: Loading docks appear on the east building face and separate trailer-yard faces on the west/south — distinct dock clusters.
fieldNotes.multipleFacilities: Brewery complex is a campus: main brewhouse/process building, tank farm structures, and adjacent warehouse/material buildings on one fenced parcel.
fieldNotes.railServed: A rail spur curves into the NW of the property with rail cars parked on it (visible in z19 imagery).
fieldNotes.urbanRural: Penn Drive industrial park at the edge of Breinigsville, surrounded by farmland and I-78; small-town/edge-of-town setting -> Rural.
fieldNotes.trailersVisible: ~170 trailers counted across the south and west drop yards in the captured imagery; approximate.

citations.claim: FY2024 10-K Properties lists Breinigsville PA ('the Pennsylvania Brewery') as one of four company-owned breweries; ~76 acres / ~1M sq ft; planned 2025 capex on PA brewery infrastructure.
Most recent FY2025 10-K on file (period ending 2025-12-27), consistent with prior Properties disclosure naming the PA brewery as company-owned.

verification.rationale: Company-owned, named in 10-K Item 2; gauntlet found only a whole-company Suntory acquisition rumor and contract-brewer (not owned-plant) capacity cuts, no sale/closure/WARN for Breinigsville.

sites.name: Cincinnati Brewery - Cincinnati OH
sites.type: Brewery / canning production facility (Over-the-Rhine; $85M canning expansion 2020 quadrupled canning capacity)
sites.dossierExcerpt:
The roster's ROOFTOP geocode (39.114319, -84.522324) landed directly on the
brewery complex. Satellite probing (z17-z20) confirmed a dense industrial
complex with extensive brewing process equipment, tank/silo clusters, and
multi-story manufacturing buildings — the unmistakable signature of a production
brewery. Web research confirms 1625 Central Parkway is the former Schoenling /
Hudepohl-Schoenling plant, acquired by Boston Beer in 1997 and operated as the
Samuel Adams Cincinnati Brewery; the company invested $85M in 2020 to quadruple
canning capacity. The attached taproom is at 1727 Logan St on the same block.

fieldNotes.truckGate: No controlled truck gate found. Street View (2024) along Logan St and the side streets shows the brewery's trailer/dock yards as open paved lots that meet the public city streets directly with no barrier arm or sliding gate. One distant red barrier was seen far down a side street, but the brewery's own dock yards are open.
fieldNotes.guardShack: No guard booth visible at any yard entrance in 2024 Street View; access is via Over-the-Rhine city streets.
fieldNotes.backupSensitive: Tight urban site in Over-the-Rhine. Trucks maneuver and back into docks directly off narrow city streets; a queue would block public streets. The 2020 $85M project explicitly funded 'new routes for trucks when on-site,' confirming constrained truck geometry.
fieldNotes.drivewayShort: No deep internal approach; trucks come straight off city streets into short dock aprons.
fieldNotes.dropYard: An open paved trailer-storage lot on the NW side holds rows of parked trailers (multiple carriers seen: Pegoda, City Bash) — a real drop yard, though urban and ungated.
fieldNotes.dockDoors: ~16 dock doors estimated along the building faces fronting the trailer yard; tightly packed urban building makes exact count hard. Approximate.
fieldNotes.multipleFacilities: Multi-building complex occupying roughly two city blocks: main brewhouse with extensive process equipment, canning building, tank structures, and the attached taproom block.
fieldNotes.railServed: No rail spur runs into the property; urban infill site with no rail access.
fieldNotes.urbanRural: Located in Over-the-Rhine within the dense urban fabric of Cincinnati -> Urban.
fieldNotes.trailersVisible: ~22 trailers across the captured drop-yard and dock imagery; approximate.
fieldNotes.scale: No truck scale visible in imagery.

citations.claim: Teamsters Local 1199 filed an ULP complaint on behalf of union members at Boston Beer's Cincinnati OH brewery; an active unionized production workforce in Feb 2025 confirms current operation.
$85M Over-the-Rhine brewery expansion: two remodeled canning lines + building extensions, quadrupling Cincinnati production; 100+ new jobs (completed per later trade coverage).

verification.rationale: Boston-Beer-owned via wholly owned subsidiary Samuel Adams Brewery Company Ltd; active union workforce, 2025 hiring, completed $85M canning expansion; no closure/sale/idling/WARN found.

sites.name: Milton Brewery (Dogfish Head) - Milton DE
sites.type: Brewery / production facility (Dogfish Head main production; acquired by Boston Beer 2019)
sites.dossierExcerpt:
The roster's ROOFTOP geocode (38.770294, -75.310106) landed directly on the
brewery building. Satellite probing (z17-z20) confirmed a large production
brewery: extensive outdoor fermentation/storage tank farms, brewing process
equipment, a dedicated on-site wastewater treatment plant (large circular
clarifier) on the NE, and a green-painted multi-bay industrial building. Web
research and Dogfish Head's own site confirm 6 Cannery Village Center as the
Milton main production brewery (acquired by Boston Beer in 2019). Street View
also surfaced interior brewery imagery (400-BBL fermentation tanks) and
Dogfish Head's signature whimsical structures, all consistent with this site.

fieldNotes.truckGate: No controlled truck gate. The brewery is set within the Cannery Village mixed-use development; trucks reach the operational yard directly from public development roads. Street View (2024) shows open road frontage with employee parking and no barrier arm or sliding gate.
fieldNotes.guardShack: No guard booth visible at any approach in Street View or satellite.
fieldNotes.shipRcvSeparate: Confirmed by web research: 'The south side of the building receives the beer line and deliveries of bottles, labels, boxes, and kegs, while packaged products load into trucks along the north' — receiving and shipping run from physically separate building faces.
fieldNotes.dockDoors: ~12 dock doors estimated; the brewery integrates loading into the building and the NE/north operational yard. Exact count is hard from overhead because docks are partly recessed. Approximate, flagged.
fieldNotes.dropArea: Small NE operational yard handles trucks/tankers; no large marked trailer-drop lot. Few trailers seen — dropArea band 0-10, dropYard FALSE.
fieldNotes.backupSensitive: Operational yard on the NE side is open paved/gravel with room to maneuver; truck approach is not pinched against a busy public road.
fieldNotes.drivewayShort: Trucks come off development roads into a short approach to the dock/yard area; no deep multi-truck queue lane.
fieldNotes.multipleFacilities: Primarily one large brewery building. A separate Dogfish Head shipping/distribution site exists at 25740 Cave Neck Rd, but that is a different facility off-site; this audit is of the production brewery only. multipleFacilities FALSE for this parcel.
fieldNotes.railServed: No rail spur into the property; site borders residential subdivisions and woods.
fieldNotes.urbanRural: Edge of the small town of Milton DE, surrounded by residential subdivisions, woods and ponds -> Rural.
fieldNotes.trailersVisible: Only ~3 trailers/trucks visible in captured imagery; this brewery runs lighter on-site trailer staging than the larger network sites.

citations.claim: FY2024 10-K Properties lists the Milton DE Brewery as one of four primary company-owned breweries (production + R&D + on-site taproom); spirits/spirits-RTDs produced at Milton.
Dogfish.com Milton Brewery page offers daily year-round Grain-to-Glass tours and a 27-tap tasting room; indicates active operation.

verification.rationale: 2019 Dogfish Head acquisition still stands; Milton named as company-owned brewery in 10-K, active 2026 PR/tours/events; only adverse item is a brand-level accounting impairment, not a divestiture or facility closure.

sites.name: Samuel Adams Boston Brewery - Jamaica Plain, Boston MA
sites.type: Brewery / production facility (heritage Jamaica Plain site; smaller footprint, taproom-attached)
sites.dossierExcerpt:
The roster's ROOFTOP geocode (42.314544, -71.102795) landed on the brewery roof
(solar-paneled). Apple Maps lists 42.3144329, -71.1031187 — essentially the same
building, a few meters west. Satellite probing (z18-z20) and Street View
confirmed the historic Haffenreffer brewery complex: brick industrial buildings
with a cupola, a corrugated-metal warehouse section, and a solar-panel roof.
Web research and Boston Beer's own site confirm 30 Germania St as the original
Samuel Adams Boston Brewery — now the company's research-and-development
brewhouse with an attached visitor taproom. Street View interior imagery shows
fermentation tanks, kegs, and bourbon barrels — a working pilot brewery.

fieldNotes.truckGate: No truck gate. This is a small heritage R&D brewery and taproom inside the historic Haffenreffer brewery complex in Jamaica Plain. Access is via narrow public residential streets; only small surface parking lots are present. No barrier arm, sliding gate, or checkpoint.
fieldNotes.guardShack: No guard booth — small surface parking lots with painted 'PARKING' markings; visitor taproom entrance with outdoor seating. No security structure.
fieldNotes.backupSensitive: Extremely tight urban site embedded in Jamaica Plain residential fabric. Any delivery vehicle maneuvers on narrow public streets; a truck would block the street. Backup-sensitive by geometry, though only box trucks/vans realistically serve this site.
fieldNotes.drivewayShort: No internal approach lane; delivery vehicles come straight off the street.
fieldNotes.dockDoors: ~2 service/loading doors at most; this is an R&D brewhouse and taproom, not a distribution facility. Band 0-10. Approximate.
fieldNotes.dropArea: No trailer drop area — no trailer parking on the site at all.
fieldNotes.multipleFacilities: The Boston Beer footprint here is a contiguous brewery+taproom occupancy within one historic complex (shared with other tenants). Treated as a single facility -> FALSE.
fieldNotes.railServed: No rail; dense urban residential neighborhood.
fieldNotes.urbanRural: Jamaica Plain, within the dense urban fabric of Boston -> Urban.
fieldNotes.trailersVisible: No tractor-trailers on site; this heritage R&D brewery does not run a trailer yard. Deliveries are by box truck/van.

citations.claim: Official Samuel Adams taproom listing shows the Boston Brewery (30 Germania St, Jamaica Plain) currently open daily with 16 taps; home to the company's R&D / innovation brewhouse.

verification.rationale: Operating, company-owned R&D brewery + taproom; confirmed by official taproom page and active 2026 careers reqs at the JP site; only 'closed' hit was the unrelated Doyle's Cafe. FREIGHT FLAG: ~2.4 acres, ~2 dock doors, no trailer yard, negligible freight-yard relevance.

sites.name: Angry Orchard Innovation Cidery - Walden NY
sites.type: Cidery / production facility (company-owned 60-acre apple orchard + Innovation Cider House; specialty/small-batch cider production)
sites.dossierExcerpt:
The roster's geocode (41.590198, -74.223894, GEOMETRIC_CENTER) is the parcel
center; the cider house building itself is ~120 m WSW at 41.5901, -74.2240.
Satellite probing (z16-z20) confirmed a distinctive timber-frame building with
an octagonal/round-roofed tasting-room section, outdoor seating areas with
picnic tables and umbrellas, and parking lots — set in the middle of a large
apple orchard (regular rows of trees). Street View surfaced interior imagery of
the cider house showing fermentation tanks and barrel-aging in a timber-frame
hall. Web research (I Love NY, NY Gov, Cider Culture) confirms 2241 Albany Post
Road as Angry Orchard's Innovation Cider House — a 15,000 sq ft small-batch
cidery, tasting room, and hard-cider R&D center on a company-owned 60-acre
orchard, opened 2018 with a $9.1M investment and ~7 full-time employees.

fieldNotes.truckGate: No truck gate. The Innovation Cider House sits in the middle of a company-owned apple orchard reached by a long winding private driveway off Albany Post Road. The driveway is open with no barrier arm, sliding gate, or checkpoint. The orchard is ringed by agricultural deer fencing, not a security fence.
fieldNotes.guardShack: No guard booth — the only structure is the 15,000 sq ft timber-frame cider house with a tasting room and small-batch production. This is a hospitality/destination + R&D facility.
fieldNotes.dockDoors: At most ~1 service/loading door for ingredient and supply deliveries; no dock apron or dock bank. This is not a distribution facility. Band 0-10, flagged.
fieldNotes.dropArea: No trailer drop area and no trailer parking on the site.
fieldNotes.drivewayShort: Truck approach is the private driveway into the cidery; short, single-lane, no queue lane.
fieldNotes.backupSensitive: Wide open rural site with large parking lots and ample maneuvering room; not pinched against a busy road.
fieldNotes.connectivityIssue: Rural orchard in Walden NY, set back from Albany Post Road and surrounded by orchard, farmland and woods. Cellular coverage may be moderate; flagged medium-confidence in uncertainFields.
fieldNotes.multipleFacilities: One main cider house building plus a couple of small ancillary farm structures; treated as a single facility -> FALSE.
fieldNotes.urbanRural: Rural orchard at the edge of the small village of Walden, surrounded by farmland and woods -> Rural.
fieldNotes.trailersVisible: No tractor-trailers on site. Most Angry Orchard production volume is at the Cincinnati brewery; Walden is a small-batch / R&D / specialty cider and visitor destination, so it does not run a freight trailer yard.
fieldNotes.siteAreaAcres: Perimeter box approximates the deer-fenced orchard/cidery parcel (~60-acre planted orchard plus grounds); ~75.6 acres as boxed.

citations.claim: Establishes the Walden NY facility as Angry Orchard's (Boston Beer Co.) company-owned 60-acre orchard + Innovation Cider House at 2241 Albany Post Rd; confirms ownership/identity.
Cider house open and operating; most recent visitor reviews May 2026, no closure, current Thu-Sun hours. (corroborating only)

verification.rationale: Company-owned and operating per 2016 opening PR + current-dated tourism/review corroboration with no closure or divestiture; capped to probable because the only current-operation evidence is Tier-3 (angryorchard.com cider-house page is age-gated). FREIGHT FLAG: hospitality/R&D agritourism destination, no real trailer yard; commercial Angry Orchard production is at Cincinnati. Not a YardFlow freight target.
